notes: Parity obstruction: if A is a locally finite union of lines and B a compact graph with finitely many C1 edges, and |A ∩ gB| = n for all rigid motions g, then n is even (odd-degree vertices of B give walls where N changes parity; even-degree B is a bounding mod-2 cycle meeting each line evenly). So the parallel-lines example has no odd-n analogue among finite unions of arcs; odd n needs a non-curve-like set. Outside Lean: the whole argument (plane topology).

sources.cite: Croft-Falconer-Guy, Unsolved Problems in Geometry, G9
S. Jackson, R. D. Mauldin, On a lattice problem of H. Steinhaus, JAMS 15 (2002)
